verdict: Avoid new sponge iron and ferro alloy exposure in Rourkela for now; only lend to integrated, cash-generative units with clean compliance records, and only against tight structural safeguards.
title: Rourkela sponge iron & ferro alloys: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Sponge iron and ferro alloys are conversion businesses: you buy iron ore, coal and power, run them through a kiln or furnace, and sell a commodity priced off scrap and steel.** Cash is made on the spread between input cost and realisation, not on brand or customer loyalty. Shyam Metalics' March 2026 sponge iron realisation was Rs 25,656 per MT, up 1.98% YoY, while volumes fell 2.33% to 81,083 MT [5][6] — so price moved but tonnage did not. **When a proposal lands, check the unit's own realisation and volume trend; if volumes are flat or falling while the borrower projects growth, ask for the customer-wise dispatch register.**

## Where cash sits and what has changed
**Working capital is the whole game: ore and coal inventory, power bills, and receivables from steel traders.** Peer liquidity has historically been thin — Agrawal Sponge ran average working capital utilisation of ~91% for the twelve months to Sep 2018 [10], and that report is old, so treat it as a pattern, not a current fact. On the ground, villagers in Balanda have petitioned the CM against polluting firms and the OSPCB issued show-cause notices to five units [1]; in March 2025 the SPCB served closure notices on 11 polluting industrial units [3]. **So when a proposal lands, check the unit's consent-to-operate status and any pending SPCB notice; if there is an open show-cause or closure notice, decline.**

## Where the growth is
**The opportunity is in the supplier ring around the anchors, not in another kiln.** The CM launched 20 industrial projects worth Rs 8,884 crore in Rourkela and signed 22 MoUs worth Rs 43,349 crore expected to generate 18,985 jobs [2], with a stated strategy of building MSMEs around anchor industries as fabricators, logistics partners and maintenance providers [2]. **Pursue fabricators, maintenance contractors and logistics units with anchor-company purchase orders; avoid standalone sponge iron units with no captive power and no long-term ore linkage.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the commodity cycle: keep tenor short, insist on a cash-flow-based limit rather than a turnover multiple, and covenant on debt-service cover and promoter contribution.** Peer results show the cycle is real — Shyam Metalics' Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin was 12.2% with PAT up only 0.1% YoY [7], and ICRA flags that a large debt-funded capex or a significant weakening of earnings can trigger a downgrade [8]. **Take stock statements, power bills, GST returns and a quarterly SPCB compliance certificate every month; if any one is missing twice, freeze the limit.**
watch: Open show-cause or closure notice -> decline or exit the account
Sponge iron realisation and dispatch volume (monthly)
Realisation falling while volumes flat -> reprice the limit and seek promoter support
GST turnover below bank credits by more than 20% -> investigate diversion before renewal
Consumption per tonne rising -> check kiln shutdowns and ask for maintenance records
